tb21_profile.skill: Git object-database forensics: find a secret that survives a history rewrite in unreachable objects/reflog/packs, then surgically purge every copy of it without disturbing unrelated files or commit messages
tb21_profile.domain: Git internals - objects, refs, reflog, dangling blobs, packfiles, filter-branch/filter-repo, gc --prune; secret leak remediation
tb21_profile.task_form: recover-deleted-data followed by a surgical repair/rewrite, verified by the absence of any trace

TMax-15K.reason: A token was committed then removed in a later commit; recover the exact string from history and write it to secret.txt - TB2.1's part 1 verbatim.
The commit was wiped by a hard reset but not yet gc'd; find the right blob among the dangling objects and restore it - the same unreachable-object hunt.
File staged then lost to a hard reset must be recovered as a dangling blob by inspecting .git directly, not with porcelain.
A hard-deleted branch's content must be found through reflogs, deleted commits or dangling blobs; teaches all three recovery routes.
A config.json holding SECRET_KEY was committed then deleted; recover it from history and report the secret value.
Deleted config.key must be dug out of the Git history and its exact contents reported; same recover-a-secret-from-a-past-commit core.
Hardcoded telemetry token added in an old commit and later removed; extract just the token string into a file.
A deleted script must be reconstructed from traces left in the repository's reflog; reflog archaeology is the transferable part.
Search the Git history to recover a deleted env file and restore it; straightforward history search, no unreachable-object work.
Git forensics to recover a lost credential, bundled with unrelated build and concurrency fixes that dilute it.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Both halves of this task: locate the dangling commit that added secret.key in the bare repo, and remove that commit from the history.
Force-push the removal, then prove it with the reflog entry showing the reset and the short SHA of the offending commit.
Preserve the bad commit on a side branch first, then rewrite history to remove secret.key and prove the two states are consistent.
Identify the exact commit that introduced secret.key before rewriting, then prove from a fresh clone that it is gone.
Permanently remove a secret file from history and verify by checksum manifest that it is absent while every other file survives.
Forensics on a packed repository using only verify-pack and cat-file: you need exactly this to prove a secret blob is not hiding in a packfile.
Build a commit from blobs and trees with plumbing only; the object-model fluency needed to rewrite history by hand.
Identify a pre-rewrite tip solely from the reflog rather than by guessing a relative ref; reading the reflog as evidence.
Documents a force-push with the reflog entries that prove what history used to be; same evidence trail a rewrite leaves.
Dump commit and tree objects with cat-file -p; the basic object inspection used to walk back to a hidden blob.

A secret survives in a lower image layer despite attempts to delete it; same insight that removal at the tip does not erase history.
Construct a commit using only plumbing commands: hash-object, write-tree, commit-tree, update-ref - the toolkit for hand-rewriting history.
Drive the original git binaries (init-db, write-tree, commit-tree) to build an object database; forces object-model reasoning with no porcelain.
Second plumbing-only commit-construction variant; same object-model skill, slightly different framing.
Install a gitleaks pre-commit hook that scans staged changes for secrets; the detection side of secret-leak handling.
Split a diff hunk and fold only part of it into an existing patch: surgical history editing that must leave the rest untouched.
Attach and verify git notes against rebuilt artifacts; touches the object database but not reachability or rewriting.
Walk every branch, commit and file version to render them out; practice enumerating everything a repository still contains.

Filesystem id derivation breaks when the repo has no SCM; forces reasoning about what identifies a repository.
Subrepo dependency objects initialise wrongly; nested-repository bookkeeping, adjacent to walking a repo's real contents.
VCS clone path is broken; only touches the outside of git, no object-level work.
Repository loading fails when metadata is missing; repository-handling code, but nothing about history.
SecretsManager filters return nothing; shares the word secret and a filtering bug, little else - listed to fill the ten.
A missing helper in the add path of a content-addressed data tool; weakest of the ten, included only for corpus coverage.

reset_index is broken; requires knowing exactly what the index, tree and working copy should each contain after a reset.
Object store lacks pack-data support; packfile handling is precisely where a supposedly deleted blob keeps hiding.
Annotated tag creation fails; exercises building and writing a real Git object with correct headers.
describe on a tagless repository ignores abbrev; walking history and refs to name a commit.
Config parsing error surfaces while writing the reflog during clone; touches the reflog machinery directly.
Commit author-date parsing throws on real repositories; reading raw commit-object headers correctly.
Cannot pass the environment git-commit-tree needs; driving plumbing commands with controlled identity, as a history rewrite must.
History mining between tags across repositories is broken; systematic traversal of commit history to find what it contains.

Secret committed then removed in a later commit; recover the exact token from history and write it to secret.txt.
Locate the dangling commit that added secret.key in the bare repo and remove that commit from history: both halves of this task.
Commit wiped by a hard reset but not yet gc'd; identify the right blob among the dangling objects and restore it.
Remove the commit that added secret.key from the repository's history so the file is gone for good.
Rewrite to drop the secret commit and prove it with the reflog entry and short SHA of the offending commit.

Preserve the offending commit, then force-push a rewritten history without secret.key and reconcile the two states.

notes: This query is unusually well served. RTS contains a very large near-duplicate family (300+ docs) of 'remove the commit that added secret.key from github.com/jrogue/sample.git' - genuinely on-target, so I kept the five richest variants (the ones that also require finding the dangling commit, reflog evidence, or proving absence from a fresh clone) rather than ten clones; the merge step should be aware that dozens more interchangeable siblings exist and that picking many of them would add no diversity. tw_6480 and tw_329715 came from my own searches, not the shortlist, and are the two best single candidates in the pool. SWE-Rebench's dulwich family (8 tasks, a pure-Python Git implementation) is the only place outside TMax/RTS/TW that teaches the object model itself. SWE-Smith has essentially nothing on Git internals; its ten are scored honestly low, with the two stackprinter secret-censoring bugs the only real skill link.
